questions.explain: Metals and graphite conduct; plastic, rubber and dry wood don't.

questions.prompt: Why are electric wires made of copper covered in plastic?
options: Copper conducts the current; plastic insulates to keep us safe
questions.explain: The conductor carries the current; the insulator prevents shocks and short circuits.

questions.prompt: In the conductor tester, pencil lead made the bulb glow, but dimly. What does this tell you?
options: Graphite conducts, but not as well as metals
questions.explain: Graphite is a non-metal that conducts, but with more resistance than copper.

questions.prompt: Which are SAFE practices with electricity at home? Choose all that apply.
options: Never touching switches with wet hands
Not overloading one socket with many plugs
Poking a screwdriver into a socket to test it
Replacing damaged wires with insulated ones
Flying kites near overhead power lines
questions.explain: Water conducts; overloading overheats; power lines can kill.

questions.prompt: Why do electricians wear rubber gloves and shoes?
options: Rubber is an insulator, so current can't pass through their body to the ground

questions.prompt: Pure water is a poor conductor, but tap water and salt water conduct. What explains this?
options: Tap and salt water contain dissolved salts that carry charge
questions.explain: Dissolved salts allow current to flow, which is why wet hands are dangerous.

questions.prompt: Each year, many people in India are injured by electric shocks, for example from hanging clothes on wires or using damaged cables during the monsoon. Suggest a safety campaign for your school: three key messages and how you would share them.
questions.modelAnswer: Messages: 1) Never touch switches, plugs or appliances with wet hands: water conducts electricity. 2) Report and replace damaged, bare or sparking wires; never use them. 3) Stay away from fallen power lines and never hang clothes on electric wires, especially in the monsoon. Sharing: posters near taps and switches, a short skit in assembly, a demonstration with a conductor tester using safe 1.5 V cells, and messages to parents on the school app.
rubric: Each linked to conductors or insulators
A realistic way to share them
questions.explain: Criterion D: use science to protect your community.

questions.text: Materials that allow current to pass through are ___; materials that do not are ___.
questions.explain: Conductors and insulators are both essential in every circuit.
